I1.evidence: The code is written in open, formal, widely shared languages: OxCal's model language ('implemented in OxCal', l. 267) and R using the ArchaeoPhases package ('R code for tempo and occurrence plots', l. 560-561).

I2.evidence: No FAIR vocabulary or ontology is evidenced for the code artefacts.

I3.evidence: Dependencies have qualified references: 'functions provided by ArchaeoPhases software (Philippe & Vibet, 2020)' (l. 528-529), cited with JSS DOI 10.18637/jss.v093.c01 (rendered with a doubled https://doi.org/ prefix, l. 690-691) and as 'the CRAN package ArchaeoPhases'. R1.evidence: The code's function is richly described: model structure (two sections, l. 268-270); the MCMC tallying procedure for the Allen relations and mode probabilities (l. 327-336); scripts that reproduce Figs 3 and 4; and the Supplement describes five independent runs (l. 272-273) and the 54-relation probability tests (l. 447-449).

R1_1.evidence: Same R1.1(a) analysis as for data. The scripts have no licence of their own; the publisher-hosted supplement inherits the version-of-record terms, and the pack lists only Elsevier TDM and STM sharing-policy URIs, none of which is a clear usage licence. CC-BY-NC-ND covers only the accepted-version repository copy, and the more restrictive publisher terms govern.

The model's derivation from the Bayliss et al. 2013 prior is stated with each change (l. 247-260), and the versions are OxCal 4.4.2 and IntCal20.

R1_3.evidence: The authors' scripts show no package structure, CITATION.cff, CodeMeta, or community review. ArchaeoPhases' CRAN and JSS status belongs to a third-party dependency and cannot substitute for the authors' scripts.

barriers: Closed monograph (Tier 3): Hines & Bayliss (eds.) 2013 Society for Medieval Archaeology print monograph, which holds Bayliss et al. 2013 Table 7.18, the constraint pages (pp. 339-345, 449-450), and Nielsen 2013 identifications. The paper states that the chronological prior is the OxCal model deposited in the ADS project archive, so the encoded constraints are probably also reachable via Tier 0.
Possible paywall (Tier 2): Hines 2021, the Antiquaries Journal article that sources the RAF Lakenheath additions; the paper gives no DOI, so access needs manual retrieval and table extraction.
Not enumerated, recorded for transparency: the acknowledgements thank John Hines for 'supplying a copy of the Lakenheath report' (privately supplied). It is not referenced in Methods/Results.

Record-weighted coverage is not feasible because the paper does not give per-source record counts.

A1.evidence: Coverage is substantial (4/5 enumerated datasets at Tier 0-2 = 80%), so the A1 completeness override does not apply. The principal Supplement is delivered over HTTPS via the article landing page (Row 6 entitlement). The upstream ADS dataset resolves via DOI (pack: http_status 200, state findable).

A1_1.evidence: HTTPS delivery through the article landing page (Row 6) and DOI resolution for the upstream ADS archive. Both are open, free, universally implementable protocols.

A1_2.evidence: No access restriction is documented or warranted. The data are radiocarbon determinations and bead-type occurrences from early medieval graves, with no CARE or human-subject restriction, and the paper states 'Data and materials are available in the Supplement.' The v2.1 open case applies: a fully open resource needing no authentication satisfies A1.2.

A2.evidence: Row 6: supplement-only deposits get A2 = 0. There is no independent metadata record that would persist if the supplement became unavailable.

F1.evidence: Principal data artefact is the publisher-hosted Supplement: 'Data and materials are available in the Supplement' (l. 566); the revised OxCal model 'comprises two sections; the first defines the likelihoods and their constraints, and the second defines occurrences for each of the bead types' (l. 268-270). Distributed under article DOI 10.1016/j.jas.2023.105765, so F1 = 1 under the supplement-under-article-DOI rule. Upstream ADS archive has its own DOI 10.5284/1018290.

F2.evidence: Supplement-only deposit with no independent metadata record: platform table Row 6 gives F2 = 0. The ADS upstream archive has a DataCite record but is non-principal (the revised model with the data is in the Supplement); conjunctive scoring would give 0 even if it were co-principal.

F3.evidence: Row 6: no independent metadata record carrying a supplement-level identifier. The Crossref identifier_in_metadata flag refers to the article record, not the supplement.

F4.evidence: Row 6: no registry indexing of the supplement as a resource. No independent deposit is named in the paper.

I1.evidence: The data are encoded as an OxCal model: 'The revised chronological model was implemented in OxCal and is included in the Supplement. It comprises two sections; the first defines the likelihoods and their constraints, and the second defines occurrences for each of the bead types' (l. 267-270). This is a formal, documented, machine-parseable model language widely shared in the radiocarbon community. The upstream source is 'a relational database' (l. 222).

I2.evidence: Bead types follow the Brugmann (2004)/Nielsen (2013) classification codes (e.g. BE1-Koch20, BE3-Amber). This is a published typology, but the paper shows no FAIR vocabulary with PIDs or machine-readable URIs (no PeriodO, Getty AAT, or similar).

I3.evidence: The derivation relation is stated with a PID: 'Chronological relations among the female graves are based on a chronological prior from the OxCal model deposited in the project archive (Hines, 2013)' (l. 232-234). The source is cited as 'Hines, J. (2013) ... [data-set]. Archaeological Data Service. https://doi.org/10.5284/1018290'. The pack confirms that DOI resolves to the ADS Dataset.

R1.evidence: The data are richly described: 72 female graves (52 from the Hines & Bayliss project, 20 from RAF Lakenheath; l. 212-219); 23 named bead types (Fig. 4); model structure (likelihoods/constraints; occurrences); retained stratigraphic and known-age constraints (l. 236-247); and the Supplement documents five independent runs (l. 272-273).

R1_1.evidence: The Supplement has no licence of its own, so under R1.1(a) the article licence extends to it. The pack's Crossref record for the version of record lists only publisher TDM and sharing-policy URIs (elsevier.com/tdm/userlicense/1.0, elsevier.com/legal/tdmrep-license, STM 10.15223/policy-004/-012/-017/-029/-037). None is a clear data-usage grant, so this is functionally all-rights-reserved. The cover sheet's CC-BY-NC-ND governs only the White Rose accepted-version copy; under the most-restrictive rule for the same artefact, the publisher terms govern.

R1_2.evidence: Provenance is detailed. Sources: Hines 2013 ADS model, Hines 2021 Lakenheath additions, Nielsen 2013 identifications. Transformations: constraints retained (Castledyke, Dover Buckland, Edix Hill, and Melbourn stratigraphy; BU2-d/h buckle after AD 510; Dagobert I coin after AD 629) and three constraints removed with rationale (l. 247-260). Software: 'OxCal version 4.4.2 and the IntCal20 calibration curve' (l. 270-271).

R1_3.evidence: Publisher supplement with no deposit-level standard (no DataCite record and no domain schema such as ARIADNEplus or CIDOC-CRM). OxCal and IntCal20 are methodological standards and are excluded. The ADS route (c) would apply only to the non-principal upstream archive; conjunctive scoring would still give 0.
